title: Connection wakeback and fairness safeguard for transient KV pressure
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: In a recent incident we observed a class of failures where nodes under transient KV pressure left a subset of in-flight tenant connections in a zombie/waiting state. Those connections held priority tokens and caused short SLO blips for high-priority customers during regional evictions. This PR introduces a lightweight reconciling probe ("wakeback") that opportunistically revalidates connection liveness after an eviction/rejoin window and a fairness-safeguard that temporarily demotes aggressive tenants when KV pressure is detected, preventing long tail SLO violations.

What this does (single-line checklist):
- Adds a connection wakeback probe that runs on connection reattach and periodic background windows.
- Implements a transient fairness-safeguard that reduces priority score for tenants exhibiting repeated KV-induced stalls.
- Emits new telemetry and tracing spans for wakeback operations and fairness demotions.
- Adds unit and integration tests covering race cases and recovery flows.
- Provides a controlled rollout plan and a fast rollback path (feature flag + runtime kill switch).

Technical highlights:
- Wakeback is implemented as a short-lived health handshake (idempotent) that validates KV cache coherence and connection liveness before reassigning priority tokens. It avoids heavy rebuilds by reusing the existing KV prefix snapshot when safe.
- Fairness-safeguard computes a short sliding window score derived from KV stall counters and request latency percentiles; if a tenant exceeds the configured threshold, its priority weight is multiplied by a dampening factor for a configurable period (default 30s).
- Telemetry: metric names introduced: redwood.conn_wakeback.attempts, redwood.conn_wakeback.success, redwood.safeguard.demotions, redwood.safeguard.windows_skipped. Traces include wakeback.start and wakeback.resolve with tenant id tag.
- Rollout: gated behind runtime flag runtime.conn_wakeback.enabled and runtime.safeguard.enabled. Default is off for 1.0 rollout canary; ops runbook included.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for orchestrator and allocator race paths.
- Integration test simulating KV stall with synthetic latency injection and verifying demotion + recovery.
- Manual canary in us-west-2 with heartbeat monitoring for 2 hours; no SLO regressions observed in the canary window.

Checklist (completed):
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Telemetry wired and dashboards updated
- [x] Runbook + rollback instructions added
- [x] Metrics smoke pass in canary

Notes and alternatives considered:
- We evaluated a full connection drain strategy but it was too disruptive for high-throughput tenants and caused longer KV misses. Wakeback preserves in-flight progress where safe.
- We also considered per-node backoff vs tenant-level demotion; tenant-level gives better fairness across noisy neighbors.

Merge: squashed after CI green and sign-off.

release_notes: Introduces a non-default 'connection wakeback' probe and a transient fairness safeguard to reduce SLO blips caused by KV pressure. Feature gated and rolled out behind runtime flags; no customer-facing API changes.
additional_context: This change was prompted by incident SUP-7212. The approach prioritizes minimal disruption for high-throughput tenants while improving fairness under transient backend pressure. Ops playbook includes metric thresholds for auto-disabling the feature during anomalous regressions.
